name: Build-up baiting / provocation football
scopeNote: Exemplar Roberto De Zerbi: Sassuolo (2018-06-13 to 2021-05-23, last league match; dates from search summaries, not page-verified), Brighton (2022-09-16 to 2024-05-19) and Marseille (2024-06-30 to 2026-02-11; no Marseille-specific tactical page was mined, so Marseille is counted for dates only). Core term used by sources: 'press-baiting' / 'studs-on-the-ball' / 'artificial transitions' (Premier League), 'enticement' (Analytics FC), 'provoking the opposition press' (Sky). The idea is: slow, short build-up with the goalkeeper as an extra defender and a deep double pivot to lure the press, then a quick break through it into the space behind. It is not tiki-taka or Guardiola-style positional play: sources contrast it with City (control and rest defence) and say De Zerbi himself is not 'De Zerbismo'. Sources also stress it is not unique to him and depends on the opponent actually pressing. Shakhtar (2021-22) and Spurs (from 2026-03-31) are excluded.
openQuestions: Proposed ids not yet in the catalog: manager 'roberto-de-zerbi' and teams 'brighton-de-zerbi', 'sassuolo-de-zerbi' (no De Zerbi/Brighton/Sassuolo/Marseille files in profile-audit/research/manager or team at time of search). Confirm before building exemplars.

Spell dates need a second source: Sassuolo appointment 2018-06-13 and Sassuolo end ~2021-05-23 (search summary only; Shakhtar announced him 2021-05-25); Brighton appointment 2022-09-16 (first press conference about 2022-09-20, per Sky 'just over two weeks' before 2022-10-08); Brighton mutual termination announced 2024-05-18, set to 2024-05-19; Marseille appointment 2024-06-30 (beIN) and exit 2026-02-11 (mutual agreement after 5-0 loss to PSG, per ESPN/beIN search summaries).
Marseille 2024/25 (Ligue 1 runner-up) has no mined Marseille-specific tactical page; the Ligue1.com piece is a pre-season Brighton 2023/24 data profile.

Credit contested: Premier League and Analytics FC treat baiting as De Zerbi's signature, while search summaries note other pieces argue every team baits pressure and that De Zerbi rejected being credited (not located in a primary interview).

Pressing is described as man-to-man (Premier League, Left Back Football for Sassuolo's first wave) but Sassuolo also used zonal lateral pressing and a 4-4-2 medium block (Left Back Football, TFA). Sky says he called pressing 'a gamble' and prefers the opponent to press.
Analytics FC (Oct 2023) hypothesis that De Zerbi benefited from opponents choosing to press; Sporting Life (Feb 2024) notes weakness against low blocks: three wins in 16 league games.

sources.title: Timing is Everything: De Zerbi's Brighton - Analytics FC
sources.evidence: Brighton collapse their build-up structure in order to create a compact 4-2 or 4-1 structure to build out through. The compact nature of the build-up structure often draw opposition teams in, high and narrow in their press, towards Brighton's core of players.

sources.title: Timing is Everything: De Zerbi's Brighton - Analytics FC

sources.title: Timing is Everything: De Zerbi's Brighton - Analytics FC
sources.evidence: Brighton create a numerical overload in the build-up, by shunting the keeper forwards as a +1 in the backline, narrowing the fullbacks, and dropping one (or both) of the double pivot, to create a sum or six or seven players, in a small amount of space. This then draws the opposition onto Brighton.
